# Are your lien deadlines still open?

> Free calculator for the preliminary notice and lien filing deadlines a subcontractor or supplier faces in California, Texas, Florida, Arizona, Washington, Georgia and Colorado. Enter your first and last day on the job; see both dates, weekend flags, and days left. Entirely client-side, nothing uploaded.

Free to use and source available (FSL-1.1-MIT). Results are estimates from the numbers typed in, not legal, tax, financial or professional advice.

## What it covers

- Texas: one notice date per month of unpaid work (15th day of the 3rd month after it, 2nd on residential), lien affidavit 15th of the 4th (3rd) month; rules for original contracts from 2022-01-01, the same for every tier.
- Georgia: Notice to Contractor shown only for second-tier claimants (hired by a subcontractor), as the statute requires it only without privity with the contractor.
- Washington: a subcontractor hired by the prime contractor owes no notice of right to claim a lien (RCW 60.04.031(2)(c)), except on repair or remodel of an existing owner-occupied single-family home; second-tier claimants get the 60-day (10-day on a new single-family home) look-back.
- Late notices: California and Arizona protect work from 20 days before a late notice, Washington 60 (10); Florida treats a late Notice to Owner as a complete defense to the lien (713.06(2)(a)). A passed date shows the earliest work a notice served today still covers.
- California, Arizona, Florida, Colorado: the same clocks for first- and second-tier claimants.
- Each result links the statute sections it uses; timing checked against the statute text on 2026-11-25 (California's sub lien clock is Civ. Code § 8414).
